summary: Mumbai is India's financial capital and most congested city, built on a peninsula where the sea is the obvious bypass to gridlocked roads. Heavy existing RoPax demand, a government water-transport push and enormous scale make it Navier's India anchor.

use_cases.title: Congestion-relief commuting
use_cases.body: Gateway↔Mandwa (~10 nm) and Gateway↔Belapur (~12 nm) clean commuter links relieving the road network.

use_cases.title: Elephanta & harbour tourism
use_cases.body: Fast comfortable runs to the UNESCO caves (~6 nm), replacing slow launches.

use_cases.title: Konkan-coast links
use_cases.body: Long-haul coastal corridors down the Konkan coast.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Mumbai's core corridors (Gateway↔Mandwa ~10 nm, ↔Belapur ~12 nm, Elephanta ~6 nm) are short, dense and inside the all-electric envelope over sheltered harbour water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the long Konkan-coast line-haul (Mumbai↔Goa ~220 nm) and inter-city coastal corridors with no charging at intermediate ports.

competitive_landscape: Today: diesel RoPax/catamaran on Gateway–Mandwa, informal launches to Elephanta, and nascent Navi Mumbai water transport. The pain is slow, rough, weather-limited boats against catastrophic road congestion — the status quo a fast, clean tier improves on.
seasonality: SW monsoon (June–Sept) brings rough seas and service suspensions on exposed legs; harbour and sheltered corridors run most of the year with routing/scheduling around the monsoon.
regulatory_note: India's Sagarmala program and the Maharashtra Maritime Board actively promote harbour and coastal passenger water transport to relieve congestion, with an emerging maritime decarbonization agenda — a clear public pathway.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.
